strings.name: John Jumper
strings.summary: John Jumper combines physics, chemistry and machine learning and helped lead AlphaFold2, substantially improving protein-structure prediction from amino-acid sequences. The team's work drew on experimental structure databases, algorithms and engineering and supported open structural resources. He shared half the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis. Predictions guide research but still require experimental examination for particular scientific questions.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to AlphaFold's protein-structure prediction research, advancing the use of AI to understand the structures of biological molecules.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Vanderbilt bachelor's (2007); Cambridge MPhil (2008); University of Chicago chemistry PhD (2017)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: AlphaFold2
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Combined biological knowledge with deep learning in a team breakthrough at the CASP14 structure-prediction assessment.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Resources for structural research
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Helped make prediction methods and resources available to researchers, supporting faster formulation and testing of biological questions.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Announced planned move
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Said he would leave Google DeepMind and join Anthropic after a break; no start date is inferred.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Shared Nobel Prize in Chemistry
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Shared half the prize with Hassabis for protein-structure prediction; Baker received the other half.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: AlphaFold3 published
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Co-authored a method predicting structures of interactions among proteins, nucleic acids and other molecules.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: AlphaFold2 methods paper
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Co-authored the architecture and evaluation paper as a joint first author, with associated code released.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: CASP14 breakthrough
strings.timeline.event-5.text: The team substantially improved three-dimensional protein-structure predictions in the blinded assessment.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Doctorate and DeepMind
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Completed his chemistry PhD at Chicago and subsequently joined DeepMind's structure-prediction research.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Cambridge MPhil
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Studied theoretical condensed-matter physics at the Cavendish Laboratory before work on protein simulation.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Vanderbilt bachelor's degree
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed undergraduate mathematics and physics before graduate study at Cambridge.
